original_representation.quote:
EXECUTIVE ORDER
E stablishing  the  L ake  M oraine  M igra ­
to r y W aterfow l  R efuge
NORTH DAKOTA
By virtue of and pursuant to the au­
thority vested in me as President of the 
United States, it is ordered that all lands 
owned or controlled by the United States 
within the following-described area, 
comprising 320.00 acres, more or less, in 
Burleigh County, North Dakota, be, and 
they are hereby, reserved and set apart, 
subject to valid rights, for the use of the 
Department of Agriculture as a refuge 
and breeding ground for migratory birds 
and other wildlife:
Fifth Principal Meridian  
T. 143 N., R. 78 W., sec. 13, Ny2.
It is unlawful for any person to pur­
sue, hunt, trap, capture, wilfully disturb, 
or kill any bird or wild animal of any 
kind whatsoever within the limits of the 
refuge, or to enter thereon, except under 
such rules and regulations as may be 
prescribed by the Secretary of Agricul­
ture.
This reservation shall be known as the 
Lake Moraine Migratory Waterfowl 
Refuge.
F r a n k l in D  R oosevelt
T he  W h it e H ouse ,
May 10, 1939.
[No. 8123]
[F. R. Doc. 39-1606; Filed, May 10, 1939;
4:13 p. m.]

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The original has no sunset, deadline, completed assignment or cessation condition. PR2416 changed only the refuge name on1940-07-25 and is recorded as amendment, not an ending. The1950 report documents damaged structures, water loss, virtual abandonment and removal of signs under verbal instructions; it does not cancel the refuge, terminate an easement, relinquish all federal control or supply an earlier legal ending. No earlier named cessation was located in bounded number/name searches. The complete original reserves320acres in N1/2section13,T143N,R78W,Fifth Principal Meridian. PLO1704 expressly revokes EO8123 and repeats the identical Lake Moraine tract. It has no partial limiter, deferred effective date or continuing provision. Its signature date is1958-08-05; NARA editorial1958-08-04 is contradicted by the actual center-column signature. FilingAug8/publicationAug9 are separate dates. The complete3paragraph inventory includes reservation, wildlife/entry prohibition with regulatory exception, and naming. Prohibition and regulation permission apply within this refuge; neither is an independent continuing command after whole revocation. PR2416 renaming does not create a new reservation or save EO8123 authority. No independent EO8123 command remains.

savings_residuals.reason: Original subject-to-valid-rights language protects preexisting rights rather than granting surviving EO authority. PLO1704 contains no savings and states the lands are non-public lands, without a restoration/opening delay. Preexisting private rights, historical naming and independently authorized acts are not continuing EO effects under TC04/TC08. Bounded later checks found no revival or current EO-dependent residual.

research_rationale: The complete official original and primary PLO1704 establish the reservation and all dependent protection/naming provisions ended by express whole revocation on1958-08-05. Primary pages correct both the contaminated frozen original inventory and the editorialAug4date. PR2416 supplies an earlier name amendment, not first cessation; the full1950 report supplies material operational abandonment evidence, not a legal termination. Original terms contain no lapse/completion mechanism and bounded later searches locate no revival or surviving EO-dependent norm.

source.page_or_item: Slade NWR Easement District No1 report Sept-Dec1950, printedp1, PDFpage5
source.quote:
Flickertail, Lake Moraine, Wildfang and Yanktonai Refuges were
virtually abandoned during this period because of previously damaged
structures and the subsequent loss of -ymter. The stuctures are ir­
reparable with the limited appropriations for easement refuges. The
signs and posts were removed from the above refuge boundaries. On
the remaining refuges the structures were repaired or remained in a
generally good condition. Most of the refuges were reposted and
damaged signs replaced by new ones.

sources.page_or_item: Same report, Lake Moraine section, printedp3, PDFpage7
sources.quote:
VII. lAI'IE MORAINE
Ydhen this refuge was visited on October 17, the water level was
very low--ca, 3 to4 feet below the spillway—due to the washout in the
west end of the dam, as reported in the Narrative Report of August 1950.
On verbal instnuctions from F, C. Gillett, the signs and posts were re­
moved from the refuge boundaries.
